Former Navy SEAL Explains Russia’s Secret Campaign in Europe — In this deep-dive report for Kyiv Post, former US Navy SEAL Chuck Pfarrer breaks down Moscow’s hybrid warfare doctrine – from 2,000 unidentified drones probing NATO airbases and Telegram-recruited “single-use” sabotage agents, to state-sponsored assassinations in broad daylight.

Russian Soldier Sentenced to 12 Years for Raping Woman in Donetsk Region — The Prosecutor’s General Office announced that a Russian serviceman was sentenced to 12 years in prison for systematically raping a 57-year-old woman over two months, while his unit occupied a village in the Pokrovsk district. According to the prosecutors, the abuse ended in December 2025 when the serviceman was captured in combat by the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU).

Russian Mercenary Targets Ukrainian Artist in Warsaw — A Russian national allegedly recruited by Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) was plotting to assassinate Ukrainian rapper and blogger Kyivstoner in Warsaw. Polish authorities announced on Thursday, Aug. 13, that they detained the suspect on Aug. 7, before the attack could take place.

‘We’ll Warm Ourselves With the Fire of Russian Oil Refineries’: Ukraine Hits Back at Russia — Ukraine responded to a Russian post that appeared to threaten winter strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure by warning that Russian oil refineries could become targets that warm Ukrainians this winter.

‘They’re Starting to Moan’: Lavrov Threatens ‘Harsher’ Strikes — Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov rejected a ceasefire along the current front line and threatened “harsher” strikes against targets he claims support Ukraine’s military.

Putin Ordered Kremlin to ‘Destroy NATO and EU From Within’ – NYT — Moldova is emerging as a key target in Russia’s reported strategy to undermine NATO and the EU, with Western intelligence warning that Vladimir Putin could seek control of the country after Ukraine. Its strategic location, Russian troops in Transnistria, and energy vulnerabilities, make Moldova a potential launchpad for wider Kremlin aggression.

Zelensky Struggles to Find Ukraine’s Next Envoy to Trump — Ukraine is struggling to fill its ambassadorial post in Washington after Olga Stefanishyna’s dismissal, with potential candidates reluctant to take on a difficult role amid uncertainty over US policy toward Kyiv, Politico reports.

‘Only a Madman’ Would Say Sending Patriots to Ukraine Weakens Poland, Polish Minister Says — Poland has no plans yet to transfer Patriot batteries to Ukraine, Deputy Defense Minister Cezary Tomczyk said, dismissing opposition claims that such a move would leave Poland vulnerable. He argued that intercepting Russian missiles over Ukraine ultimately strengthens Poland’s security, calling the opposing argument “something only a madman would come up with.”

Mobilisation Rumours: Kremlin Under Pressure? — Russia is weighing a new mobilisation as its war effort stalls and economic pressures mount. Analysts warn it could deepen public discontent, strain Russia’s administrative system and worsen labour shortages. The Kremlin is seeking alternatives, including North Korean support, while European policymakers are urged to exploit growing tensions within Russia’s elite.

Exiled Putin Critic Says Push for Peace Put Him in Danger — Russian anti-war politician Boris Nadezhdin has fled to France after years of carefully calibrated criticism of the Kremlin. He says authorities finally crossed a line by threatening criminal charges, as growing war fatigue and calls for peace face ever harsher repression.

‘Like Snow on Your Head’: Russia Threatens Ukraine With Winter ‘Freeze’ as Kyiv Pushes for Ceasefire — Russia has threatened Ukraine with a winter “freeze,” appearing to signal more attacks as temperatures drop. The warning came just a day after Kyiv offered Moscow a mutual “freeze” on attacks against civilian targets in the Black Sea, amid escalating strikes on ports and maritime infrastructure.

Putin Has an Unexpected Ally in Ukraine’s War — Russia’s attacks are increasingly colliding with extreme heat and drought in Europe, putting pressure on Ukraine’s alternative trade, electricity, fire response and water systems, Newsweek reports.

Drone Shot Down in Latvian Airspace: Military — NATO fighter jets shot down a drone that strayed into Latvian airspace Friday, the latest sign of growing unease over drone activity across Europe. The incident came as Russia and Ukraine traded fresh drone strikes, with dozens of Ukrainian drones reportedly downed over Russia’s Leningrad region.

Russian Oil Refinery Shuts Down for Months After Ukrainian Drone Strike — A Russian oil refinery more than 1,300 kilometers from Ukraine has been completely shut down after a Ukrainian drone strike, with repairs potentially taking up to six months. The strike adds to Kyiv’s escalating campaign against Russia’s oil industry and a growing fuel crunch across the country.

Romania Starts Shutting Down Sole Working Nuclear Reactor — Romanian state-owned nuclear power producer Nuclearelectrica has started the process of disconnecting its sole working reactor from the power grid due to record low Danube river levels, it said on Thursday.

Ust-Luga Ablaze Again as 54 Ukrainian Drones Hit Russia’s Key Baltic Oil Port — Ukraine attacked Russia’s key Baltic oil port of Ust-Luga with 54 drones overnight on Aug. 14, triggering a fire and disrupting operations. The strike marks at least the sixth attack on the port this year as Kyiv intensifies efforts to hit Russia’s lucrative oil-export infrastructure.

The Danger of Empty Deterrence – the Lesson From Leipzig — Every Western security service, our militaries, and political leaders should be alarmed by the incident in Leipzig Airport, where an explosive-laden drone was positioned near a Ukrainian Antonov cargo aircraft.

‘Patriot Licenses for Ukraine are Not in America’s Interest’ | Stefan Korshak — “The Americans are not enthusiastic about arming Ukraine,” Stefan Korshak, Senior Defense Correspondent at the Kyiv Post, says in World Talks. According to him, granting Ukraine a license to produce Patriot systems would not be in the United States’ interest.

Ukraine Offers Russia Black Sea Moratorium — Ukraine has proposed a mutual halt to attacks on civilian ships and ports after striking Novorossiysk, as Russian attacks drive Ukrainian grain exports down 76%.
Russian Drone Attack Injures 3 in Cherkasy Region — Three people were injured after a Russian drone struck a residential building in the Smila community of Cherkasy region.

Putin’s New Clothes: Sinking Fleets, Staged Strength, Fear of Anti-War Millions — Putin’s military makeover comes as Russia faces naval setbacks, pressure on its shadow fleet, and signs that millions may support ending the war.

Russian Strikes Kill 1, Wound 15 in Kramatorsk as Civilian Toll Climbs — Russian strikes killed at least one person and wounded 15 in Kramatorsk, while a separate attack in Zaporizhzhia injured two more, including a child.

North Korea Threatens ‘Stronger Deterrence’ Ahead of US-South Korea Drills — North Korea threatened stronger deterrence measures as US-South Korea drills prepare forces for possible combat with troops hardened by fighting alongside Russia in Ukraine.

Poland Uncovers Russian Plot to Kill US-Ukrainian Citizen in Warsaw — Poland’s Internal Security Agency detained a Russian citizen on Aug. 7, accusing him of plotting to kill a US-Ukrainian dual national in Warsaw on behalf of Russian intelligence. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said this marks the first known case of Russia targeting an American citizen inside a NATO country.

Kyiv Condemns Putin’s Visit to Disputed Kuril Islands — Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha condemned Russian President Vladimir Putin’s visit to the disputed Kuril Islands, calling it a provocation. He urged international partners to increase sanctions and reject Russia’s claim over Japan’s territory.

Yabloko Leader Vows to Stay in Russia Despite Election Ban — On Monday, Aug. 10, Russia barred the only openly anti-war party from September’s parliamentary elections. Regardless of the court’s ruling, public support for ending the war is growing, Yabloko leader Nikolai Rybakov said, adding that he will remain in Russia and keep pushing for peace.

Ukraine Proposes Mutual Halt to Black Sea Attacks — Ukraine has offered Russia a mutual halt to attacks on civilian Black Sea targets, according to an anonymous source familiar with the matter. Moscow has not responded, as both sides trade blame over strikes disrupting global grain shipments.

Ukraine Holds Security Aid Meeting with Japan’s Outgoing Ambassador — Ukrainian authorities held a series of meetings throughout the week with Japan’s outgoing Ambassador to Ukraine, Masashi Nakagome. Discussions centered on police and lab equipment donations, heating infrastructure ahead of winter and a possible Japanese role in Ukraine’s Drone Deal initiative.

Ukrainian Drones vs NATO Training – 5 Things to Know — Ukrainian drone crews devastated a US armored force in Hohenfels’ Combined Resolve 26 exercise, highlighting NATO vulnerabilities to drone warfare and echoing similar Ukrainian successes at Hedgehog 25 and Aurora 26.

Bomb Hidden in Trash Bin Kills Russian Officer Who Defected From Ukraine — Russian reports identified the victim as Robert Shageev, a former Ukrainian naval officer who joined Russia after its 2014 occupation of Crimea.

Rozetka Co-Owner Estimates Destroyed Warehouse Losses at $70M, Contents Not Included — A Ukrainian distribution center near Kyiv belonging to top retailer Rozetka was destroyed in a Russian strike on Aug. 5. Co-Owner Iryna Chechotkina said the warehouse was worth $70 million for her company, with billions of hryvnias more in lost inventory. Noting that insurance companies cannot cover losses of this magnitude, she called on the government to grant tax deferrals to help affected businesses recove

Ukraine Receives Bodies of 261 Fallen Soldiers From Russia — Ukraine has repatriated the bodies of 261 people who Russia claims were Ukrainian servicemen. Ukrainian authorities will conduct forensic examinations and identification procedures.

Ukrainian Drones ‘Wiped Out’ US Armored Brigade in Germany’s War Games — Ukrainian drone operators repeatedly “destroyed” a 3,500-strong US armored brigade during war games in Germany, forcing exercise officials to “resurrect” vehicles so the drills could continue.

Poland to Decide on Patriot Interceptors for Ukraine ‘Within Days’ — Poland is considering sending additional Patriot air-defense missiles to Ukraine, with a decision expected within days. The move would be coordinated with the US and NATO allies amid dwindling missile stocks and rising Russian ballistic attacks. Ukraine says air-defense deliveries have sharply declined, increasing pressure on Poland and other allies to provide critical interceptors.

‘Funny Games,’ ‘The Piano Teacher’ and More: Michael Haneke Retrospective in Kyiv — From August 15 to 23, 2026, an exclusive retrospective of films by the outstanding Austrian director Michael Haneke, titled VIDEO, will be held at the “Zhovten” cinema in Kyiv. The program includes six iconic works of macabre and deep auteur cinema, including the Cannes “Palme d’Or” winners “The White Ribbon” and “Amour,” the Grand Prix winner “The Piano Teacher,” as well as the scandalous “Funny Games.” The film

Zelensky Warns Land Concessions Could Give Putin Time to Prepare Another Invasion — Ukraine has presented new peace proposals to US negotiators but has not disclosed their contents. Zelensky rejected surrendering the remaining Ukrainian-held areas of Donbas and warned that Putin could eventually target a smaller NATO state.

SBU Busts 14-Member Russian Spy Ring Targeting Ukraine’s F-16, Mirage 2000 Bases — Ukraine’s Security Service (SBU) has dismantled a 14-member Russian intelligence network accused of gathering information on airfields hosting F-16 and Mirage 2000 fighter jets. The network allegedly tracked aircraft movements, photographed military facilities and passed intelligence to Russia’s military intelligence agency, the GRU.

Wildberries Loses Goods Worth a Major Russian Region’s Annual Budget — Ukrainian strikes have severely disrupted Wildberries, destroying or damaging more than 20 warehouses and goods worth an estimated Hr.480 billion, while Russian sellers and pickup-point operators face mounting losses.

Ukraine Military Aid Surged in June Despite Long-Term Shortages: Institute — EU financing pushed military aid for Ukraine to a 15-month high in June, with Kyiv receiving €7.2 billion ($8.3 billion). But despite the surge, Europe’s long-term support remains below pre-2025 levels as the US role in arming Ukraine declines.

Ukraine Strikes Major Gazprom Refinery in Russia’s Bashkortostan, Sparks Fire — Ukrainian drones struck the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat refinery in Russia’s Bashkortostan on Aug. 13, sparking a fire and sending black smoke over the facility. The strike comes as repeated Ukrainian attacks disrupt Russian oil refineries and fuel shortages resurface across at least 16 regions.

Russia Launches 133 Drones at Ukraine Overnight, Killing Two Railway Workers — Russian forces launched 133 drones at Ukraine overnight on Thursday, with Ukrainian air defenses intercepting 111, according to the Ukrainian Air Force. Strikes hit 15 locations, while debris fell in 16 others. Two railway workers were killed when a jet-powered drone struck a passenger train locomotive in Odesa region, while five people were wounded in Dnipropetrovsk region and another in Zaporizhzhia.

Zelensky Says 5% of US Patriot Missiles Could Save Ukraine This Winter — President Volodymyr Zelensky told CNN that Ukraine urgently needs more US Patriot interceptors as Russia increases its ballistic missile attacks. He said Ukraine currently has only 1% of the US stockpile, while 5% could help Kyiv survive the winter and 10% could enable it to stop all Russian ballistic missiles.

Putin Visits Disputed Kuril Islands for First Time as Russia-Japan Tensions Deepen — Putin’s first visit to the disputed Kuril Islands highlights deepening Russia-Japan tensions as Tokyo continues backing Ukraine.

Ukraine for First Time Combines 15 Weapons in Novorossiysk Strike, Expanding Black Sea ‘No-Go Zone’ — Ukraine combined 15 domestically produced weapons in a coordinated strike on Novorossiysk, hitting Russian warships and prompting authorities to declare a state of emergency in the Black Sea port city.

Karoline Leavitt to Step Down as White House Press Secretary — Karoline Leavitt will step down as White House press secretary at the end of August to focus on her family while remaining a senior outside advisor to Trump.

US Senators Press Rubio, Bessent Over 17-Month Pause in Russia Sanctions — US Senators Warren and Coons are pressing Rubio and Bessent to explain why routine Russia counter-evasion sanctions remain paused despite stalled peace talks and continued sanctions evasion.

Zelensky Says Armenia Ties Are ‘Even More Constructive’ as Putin Stays Silent on Pashinyan Victory — Zelensky and Pashinyan discussed closer Ukraine-Armenia cooperation amid growing strains between Armenia and Russia.
